info.name: RealtorIQ — Broker API v1
info.description:
The JSON API the React broker app talks to.

**The flow chains itself.** Run the Auth folder top to bottom: `Request sign-in code` saves `request_id`, `Verify code` saves `access_token` and `refresh_token`, and every other request picks the token up from collection auth. Nothing needs copy-pasting.

**Prerequisites**

1. `bin/rails db:seed` — reference data
2. `bin/rails demo:seed` — a firm you can sign into (Sethi Realty)
3. `bin/dev` — the server on :3000

**Sign-in codes are `888888` in development.** Nothing is delivered. That is a development-only bypass; the app refuses to boot in production with it set.

**Error shape.** Every failure is `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details" } }`. Switch on `code`, never on the prose. The codes are: `not_registered`, `account_disabled`, `otp_locked`, `invalid_code`, `account_suspended`, `subscription_lapsed`, `device_limit_reached`, `forbidden_role`, `rate_limited`, `delivery_failed`, `unauthorized`, `not_found`, `invalid_request`.

item.name: Leads
item.description:
The core CRM object.

**Visibility is enforced server-side.** An agent sees only leads assigned to them; managers and the super admin see the firm's whole pipeline. A lead an agent may not see returns **404, not 403** — a 403 would confirm it exists.

**Write `budget` (single amount → `budget_max`).** GET `budget_min`/`budget_max` are a filter *window* on that stored amount, not range overlap.

`missed_followup=true` is an overdue-NCD filter (not a status). `status=hot_negotiation` is hot+negotiation. Drawer params drop `q`; cards (`status`, `visited`, `missed_followup`) do not.

List returns `counts` (pipeline totals, unfiltered). Default sort is NCD NULLS FIRST. Money is raw integer rupees; the client formats lakh/crore. Screen guide: frontend/YASH.md.

request.description:
Default sort is NCD: `next_action_at ASC NULLS FIRST` (no date sits above overdue). `sort=worklist` is overdue-first.

Filters: `q` (dropped if any drawer param is set), `status` (`new` · `hot_negotiation` · codes, or `status[]=`), `visited`, `missed_followup`, drawer `name`/`mobile`/`email`/`ncd_from`/`ncd_upto`, `transaction_type`, `property_type_id`, `typology_ids[]`, `budget_min`/`budget_max` (window on stored amount), `possession_from`/`possession_to`, `source_id`, `assigned_user_id`, `sort` (`ncd` default · `worklist` · `recent` · `updated`), `page`, `per_page` (max 50).

Response includes `counts`. Saves the first lead's id for the requests below.
The design's "Missed f/u" tab. Not a status — `LEAD_STATUSES` has no such entry — but an overdue next action on a lead that isn't already dead or booked.

Every filter the leads index accepts, in one request — this is the reference for what is queryable.

Drawer params are sent without `q` because a drawer field drops `q`. GET `budget_min`/`budget_max` are a window on the stored amount (`budget`), not range overlap. `ncd_from`/`ncd_upto`, `created_from`/`created_upto` and `died_from`/`died_upto` are inclusive IST days. `died_*` matches a change into a dead status, including a lead later revived.

`property_type_id`, `source_id` and `assigned_user_id` repeat or take commas. `source_missing=true` with `source_id` is those sources plus leads with no source. A backwards date pair is 422.

`missed_followup=true` is not a real status — `next_action_at <= now` on a non-terminal lead. `status=hot_negotiation` is hot+negotiation.

`sort` is `ncd` (default, NULLS FIRST), `worklist`, `recent` or `updated`. `typology_ids` repeats as `typology_ids[]=`. `per_page` is clamped to 1..50; absent or 0 means 25. Response includes `counts` (unfiltered pipeline totals).

Creates one lead per good row and reports the rest. A bad row does not undo the rows already added. 200 returns created_count, failed_count and results. Failures include cells so the sheet can be fixed and uploaded again. A workbook, a semicolon file, a missing Mobile / Sale or rent / Budget header, or more than 200 rows is 422 and creates nothing.

Budget is whole rupees. Property type is still required for sale (Under construction or Ready possession). Location is added to the localities on the linked listings. A project code on a rent row fails. Each code cell can list at most 20 codes. A shared property links only while that firm is active. Leads are assigned to the signed-in user and start as New.

Every field the endpoint accepts, in one body.

**One lead per (firm, mobile, transaction_type).** A second sale on the same number is `422 duplicate_lead` with `details.lead_id`. Sale + rent on one number is allowed.

`notes` is Client's requirements. Optional `project_id` copies blank budget/possession/notes from that project and maps it.

**`property_type_id` is a single string, not an array.** It is permitted as a scalar, and Rails' `params.permit` *silently discards* an array value for a scalar key — so sending `["01a0…"]` arrives as nil and you get `422 Property type is required for a sale lead` with nothing pointing at the real cause. `typology_ids` **is** an array: one property type, many configurations.

**The date field is `possession_by`.** `possession_up_to` and similar near-misses are dropped in the same silent way — you get a `201` and a lead with no possession date.

`mobile` is normalised, so "97597 54343" and "+919759754343" are the same lead.

`property_type_id` is required for `sale` and forbidden for `rent`.

NCD and the opening comment are nested: `followup: { comment, next_action_at }`. Top-level `next_action_at` / `next_action_note` are ignored. `notes` is Detailed Client Requirements.

NCD and the opening comment are nested: `followup: { comment, next_action_at }`. Top-level `next_action_at` / `next_action_note` are ignored. `notes` is Detailed Client Requirements.

item.name: Uploads
item.description:
Direct upload: ask for a ticket, PUT the file straight to storage, then pass the returned `signed_id` when creating the record it belongs to.

Limits are enforced **when the ticket is issued**, per purpose — after that the browser talks to storage and this is the last point we control. Rails' own `/rails/active_storage/direct_uploads` is shadowed with a 404, since it sits outside this auth and enforces none of these rules.

`checksum` is the base64 MD5 of the file — storage rejects the PUT if it doesn't match, which is the integrity check, not a bug.

item.name: Bookings and money
item.description:
Recording a sale and the brokerage on it.

**Managers and super admins only.** An agent gets `forbidden_role` on every request in this folder, including bookings for a lead of their own.

**Net income is computed server-side and stored:**

```
round(agreement_value × commission_percent / 100) + kicker − passback
```

The design's own example is the fixture: ₹1,56,00,000 at 4.5% is ₹7,02,000, plus a ₹50,000 kicker, minus a ₹66,000 passback = **₹6,86,000** — the "₹6.86 L" on its booking screen. The client never recomputes money; `revenue` carries every line already worked out.

**Two hard blocks.** Invoices cannot exceed net income; collections cannot exceed what was invoiced, and a payment naming an invoice cannot exceed that invoice. Refusals carry the arithmetic in `error.details` so the app can explain itself.

**Cancelling** sets the booking's status and nothing else — the lead is untouched and invoices already raised stay on record.
